Oct 2, 2025 Manouk Akopyan Oct 2, 2025 1 min read Terence Crawfords confidence and aura have always been on another level, and following his win against Canelo Alvarez, it might as well be on a separate stratosphere. Terence Crawford s confidence and aura have always been at a different level, and following his unanimous decision win against Canelo Alvarez , it might as well be on a separate stratosphere. Of course there is no doubt [that I am the best fighter of this generation]. Yes definitely. No stipulations, no rehydration clause, no handicaps in any way. That was a big moment, Crawford recently said on The Jim Rome Show. It was my night. I was ready for the moment. Skills pay the bills, and I believe in my skills and abilities. I knew I was capable of beating Canelo, and that's the reason I wanted the fight. I showed the world who Terence Crawford was. Crawford attributed his success against Alvarez to his mental preparation, as he was training and shaping his physical transformation into a super middleweight since February. Terence Crawford Speaks After Defeating Canelo Alvarez & Becoming 3x Undisputed I felt real comfortable [at 168 pounds], said Crawford, whos now a five-division champion and three-weight undisputed crownholder. I've sparred a lot of big guys in my lifetime. I knew that the size wasn't going to be too much of a factor. Of course, I've never been in the ring with a guy that size before. But at the same time I believed in myself and my abilities, that I was going to be alright, and I was. Crawfords conviction and trust in his pound-for-pound abilities and skillset grew as the fight went on, and the conversation he was having with himself was whether or not he should be dialing up the pressure to further show Alvarez was not on his level. A lot of times, said Crawford. But my coach reminded me every round that 'you get close to him when you want, not when he wants to keep boxing. You don't have to get into a slugfest. POST-FIGHT BREAKDOWN | Terence Crawford's Historic Win Over Canelo Alvarez During the historic performance, Crawford mostly controlled the fight by landing 115 of 534 total punches, while Alvarez landed 99 of 338, according to CompuBox. Mar 23, 2026 0 0 Link copied! Mar 23, 2026 Manouk Akopyan Mar 23, 2026 2 min read Carlos Adames easily outpointed Austin Williams in defense of his WBC middleweight title Saturday. A day later, The Rings No. 1-ranked 160-pounder announced his move to 168. I make 160 very easily, but Ill make 168 shake even more here I come, Adames said on social media. Tell 168 that Bronco has arrived. There were many names that ran from 160 and moved up in weight, but now Im going to catch up to them. Adames (25-1-1, 18 KOs) dropped Williams (20-2, 13 KOs) in the second round and outlanded him 254 to 127, according to CompuBox, to score the victory via scores of 118-108, 117-109 and 117-109. Adames, a 31-year-old Dominican, fought as a middleweight for five years and accumulated a record of 5-0-1 with wins against Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Juan Macias Montiel, Julian Williams, Terrell Gausha and Austin Williams. Adames also fought to a highly disputed split draw with Hamzah Sheeraz in February of last year, a fight many believed Adames won. But the middleweight division is currently thin at the top, as Janibek Alimkhanuly is dealing with a PED scandal, and Cuban contender Yoenli Hernandez, ranked No. 2 by The Ring, is still nine fights into his career and on a crusade proving himself. The fighter who would benefit from Adames leaving the division is WBC interim champion Jesus Ramos, who would be elevated to full champion once the move is made official with the sanctioning body. After the fight was over against Ammo Williams, Adames said Sheeraz should seek a sequel against him. I was the one who beat him. If he wants vengeance, then he should send me the offer, said Adames. Sheeraz currently competes as a super middleweight. He last fought in July, knocking out Edgar Berlanga . Super middleweight is loaded talented fighters, including two-time undisputed champion Canelo Alvarez, who appears headed to a fight against WBC champion Christian Mbilli in September. Lester Martinez picked up the WBC interim strap on Saturday. Armando Resendez, the WBA titleholder, is set to defend his belt against Jaime Munguia on May 2. Osleys Iglesias will face Pavel Silyagin for the vacant IBF title on April 9. The Ring and WBO titles are vacant. Top-flight contenders in the division are rounded out by Sheeraz, Berlanga, Jermall Charlo, Caleb Plant, Bektemir Melikuziev, Diego Pacheco and Jacob Bank. And then there are the reputable likes of Bruno Surace, William Scull, Erik Bazinyan, Darius Fulghum, Kevin Lele Sadjo, Callum Simpson and Troy Williamson. Adames should have no shortage of options for his next fight. Everyone runs, everyone backs up. I still havent faced a fighter who comes forward. I am built to break fighters, said Adames. Sep 14, 2025 Keith Idec Sep 14, 2025 6 min read Crawford, who was undisputed champion at 140 and 147 pounds, busted up Alvarez on Saturday night and became undisputed at 168. LAS VEGAS Neither the moment nor Canelo Alvarez was too big for Terence Crawford . Two years after he tore through Errol Spence to become undisputed welterweight champ, Crawford upset Alvarez to accomplish the same feat in a division capped 21 pounds higher. It was a much more measured performance from Crawford, but he outboxed Alvarez solely from a southpaw stance and unanimously won a 12-round, 168-pound championship clash Netflix streamed worldwide from sold-out Allegiant Stadium. Judges Tim Cheatham (115-113), Max De Luca (115-113) and Steve Weisfeld (116-112) scored for Crawford, who cried after Michael Buffer announced him as the winner. Crawfords career-defining victory occurred in the biggest boxing match held in the United States since Floyd Mayweather beat Manny Pacquiao by unanimous decision in their welterweight title fight 10 years ago at nearby MGM Grand Garden Arena. Crawford (42-0, 31 KOs), who will turn 38 in two weeks, became a world champion in a fifth division before a capacity crowd of 70,482 and further cemented himself as a generational great. He is also the first male boxer in the four-belt era to be crowned undisputed champion in three weight classes (junior welterweight, welterweight and super middleweight). The Omaha, Nebraska, native accomplished what was commonly considered unthinkable a couple years ago by beating a hard-hitting, longtime super middleweight who cleaned out the 168-pound division when Crawford was the WBO welterweight champ. Crawford, who ended a 13-month layoff, often fought off his back foot, took Alvarezs power well when he got caught and picked his spots to trade with an opponent who won a light heavyweight title bout by knockout in November 2019. Canelo is a great champion, Crawford told The Ring s Max Kellerman following his impressive win. Ive got to take my hat off to him. Hes a strong competitor. Ive got nothing but respect for Canelo. Im a big fan of Canelo. He fought like a champion. Alvarez, 35, lost his Ring, IBF, WBA, WBC and WBO titles to a perceived smaller fighter who moved up 14 pounds from the junior middleweight division to challenge him. Only Mayweather, undisputed light heavyweight champ Dmitry Bivol and Crawford have defeated Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) during the Mexican legends illustrious 19-year career. Alvarez lost for the first time at super middleweight in 12 bouts. I feel great, Alvarez said. First and foremost, I want to thank everyone who came to support and has always been behind me. Im a winner for being here. There is no defeat here. Ive done everything in my career. Ive come to take risks, and thats what I did. Aug 23, 2026 Manouk Akopyan Aug 23, 2026 2 min read Rolando Romero was a man of few words after his majority decision defeat against Teofimo Lopez on Saturday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. He had no interest in talking about what had just transpired, having lost the WBA welterweight title . "I'd like to just thank my lord and savior Jesus Christ for everything in my life that I have got to enjoy. I will always be your faithful servant," Romero said before abruptly leaving the ring. Scores of 116-112 and 115-113 saw Romero (17-3, 13 KOs) beaten for the third time in little over four years, despite a third judge having it a draw at 114-114. It can definitely be argued the scorecards were generous for the now-former beltholder, who was outlanded 124-to-73 according to CompuBox. Romero enjoyed the best sequence of a mostly unspectacular fight in the fifth, stunning Lopez with a right hand and buckling his knees in the final minute of the round, 20 seconds after slicing Lopez's eyebrow with a left hook. Romero unleashed a hellacious flurry, but Lopez survived the round and immediately got back in the driver's seat for the remainder of their meeting. Romero landed double digits in punches in only one round round five according to CompuBox and lacked the urgency to stave off the surging Lopez beginning in the sixth. Even Romero's trainer Ismael Salas implored his charge to dial up the pressure to ensure victory would be within reach. During his post-fight press conference, Romero elaborated on the sequence of events that led to the loss following a career-best unanimous decision win against Ryan Garcia 15 months ago . "My immediate thoughts, look at my face. I got hit with what, two clean shots the whole fight," Romero said. "If that's enough to beat the champion, that's enough. "He never hurt me at any given moment. He got hurt multiple times throughout the fight. Every time I threw a shot, I landed it. He couldn't land anything clean on me, it was clear and apparent. "I could have pressed more. Of course, anyone can but you know, championship fights, they're all close like this, especially with two high-level fighters." Romero also elaborated on the dramatic fifth round, which saw Lopez touch the canvas during a hellacious sequence. Referee Harvey Dock ruled it a slip. "Honestly, it should have been counted as a knockdown, but you know how it is," Romero said. "He survived, knows how to survive. I hit him so many times clean and hurt him. Some of those rounds were for sure 10-8 rounds. "I was trying to open that cut even more, more than anything. I was trying to feint and land a good left hand. "I couldn't get him clean. He didn't completely wobble. The other shot I hit him with at the end of the round, though, he was out." Seven months after their initial meeting, Chris Eubank Jr. and Conor Benn headlined Tottenham Hotspur Stadium once more with a markedly different outcome than their thrilling April firefight. Dec 7, 2025 The Ring Staff Dec 7, 2025 1 min read Making his second weight jump in as many fights, now-former 130-pound world champion Lamont Roach's divisional debut was full of milestones as he withstood Isaac Cruz's early attacks to finish strong in the second-half of an absorbing interim WBC junio... Lamont Roach recovered from a third-round knockdown to outwork Isaac Cruz in the second-half of a competitive 12-round clash, but the now-former WBA 130-pound world champion didn't do enough in the judges' eyes to edge their WBC interim junior welterweight title clash. During an absorbing clash, Cruz held a narrow 87-85 edge in punches landed through five rounds, as well as scoring a 10-8 in the third frame after connecting on a left hook to leave Roach scrambling to stay upright - surrendering the first knockdown of his 11-year career. Yet after round five, the tide turned in the Maryland man's favor. Making his divisional debut at 140-pounds here, he connected on 49% of his power punches, almost doubled Cruz's landed jab tally (49-27) and had more success with round-by-round output preceding the final frame, which saw the Mexican just do enough - despite having a point deducted in the seventh. Chris Tellez scored it 115-111 for Cruz, while judges Nathan Palmer and Cory A Santos both had it 113-113 on a night neither will forget anytime soon as they look to 2026 and another potential rematch. Aug 16, 2025 The Ring Staff Aug 16, 2025 0 min read It was all too easy for Ring ambassador Hayato Tsutsumi during his Saudi showcase against Britain's Qais Ashfaq, but what did the punch stats say through three rounds? Two fights, two third-round finishes in 2025 for Ring ambassador Hayato Tsutsumi after quickly proving too hot to handle for Qais Ashfaq during their junior lightweight matchup. The 26-year-old quickly got to work against the seven-year southpaw, making the British underdog work hard during a competitive opening round evidenced by their closely-contested punch stats -- Tsutsumi threw four more total punches (24-20) and landed five more. His striking success only increased as time wore on, much to Ashfaq's drastic demise, with 17 of his 22 connected punches being credited as power punches in a second stanza which saw the 31-year-old floored and increasingly frustrated. It wouldn't last much longer. 74.1% connect percentage on power punches speaks for itself during a dominant third round and mercifully, veteran referee Leszek Jankowiak had seen enough at 2:08 of the frame. The post-fight headlines will feature viral pictures of Daniel Lapin twice hanging off the ropes like a superhero, though he won't mind. The surging Ukrainian contender came to Wembley and seized an unbeaten record while importantly keeping his own intact after a 10-round majority decision win (95-95, 96-94, 96-94) over British light-heavyweight champion Lewis Edmondson . He connected on a fight-high 24 punches in the penultimate round, having almost fallen over the top rope twice in the stanza beforehand. Such was their messy affair, it shouldn't be a surprise to know Lapin only landed 30 power punches up to the seventh round - though excelled when he needed to under duress, outlanding The Saint 39-13 over the last six minutes.
